hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: An index is dominant if its value exceeds the average of all elements to its right.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Maintain the running sum of elements to the right as you iterate backwards from the end of the array.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Compare the element against the right sum divided by the number of elements to the right.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def countDominantIndices(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(nums)
    if n <= 1:
        return 0
    ans = 0
    right_sum = 0
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        right_count = n - 1 - i
        if right_count > 0 and nums[i] * right_count > right_sum:
            ans += 1
        right_sum += nums[i]
    return ans
```

complexity.notes: A single backward pass maintains the running suffix sum in linear time.
